# Rosalind Penrose

## Overview

- **Age:** forty-five  <sub>[v2 c21 P34](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0034), [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045)</sub>
- **Origin:** Welby  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045)</sub>

## Appearance

Rosalind is a tiny woman with an almost youthful face, rosy cheeks, sweet lips, dimples, and wood-brown eyes containing tiny flecks of gold. Her hair is thick, wavy, and snow-white, arranged in flattering puffs and coils. She is known as a person who never ages and retains a bright complexion alongside her lovely appearance. She often wears flattering, young-looking attire such as delicate cream muslin adorned with light roses.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P45](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0045), [v2 c22 P2](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0002), [v2 c22 P6](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0006), [v3 c23 P3](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0003)_

## Personality

Rosalind has a playful and imaginative nature, enjoying games of "pretending" and behaving far younger than her age. She displays a distinct lack of concern for standard dietary rules or social norms, flouting kitchen rules alongside her young handmaiden. Though eccentric and prone to withdrawing from social life, she is warm, affectionate, and deeply grieves the inevitable departure of friends.

_Sources: [v2 c21 P54](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0054), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010), [v2 c27 P29](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0029), [v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032)_

## History

Rosalind lived at Echo Cottage, an ancient stone structure in Welby built by her grandfather, where she spent years living out of the public eye following her mother's death. She formed a close friendship with Nell Harcourt, frequently hosting tea parties and evenings of lighthearted pretend at her cottage. After twenty-five years of separation following a youthful betrothal quarrel, Stephen Stanhope returned, rekindling their romance and walking through the forest together while handmaiden Belinda the Fourth took over household preparations. The two were married in an informal ceremony in her honeysuckle arbor, witnessed by friends and neighbors. Following their wedding, Rosalind and Stephen relocated to Boston and traveled to the Pacific coast before establishing their new home, where she formed a close bond with her stepson Cedric.

_Sources: [v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007), [v2 c23 P10](../source/v02-c23.md#nw-v02-c23-p0010), [v2 c30 P12](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0012), [v2 c30 P29](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0029), [v2 c30 P30](../source/v02-c30.md#nw-v02-c30-p0030), [v3 c1 P2](../source/v03-c01.md#nw-v03-c01-p0002), [v3 c7 P48](../source/v03-c07.md#nw-v03-c07-p0048), [v3 c23 P3](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0003)_

## Background by volume

- named by her father after his love for the fragrance of lavender  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>
- considered a great beauty in her youth  <sub>[v2 c22 P3](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0003)</sub>
- was engaged to Stephen Stanhope twenty-five years ago before a quarrel separated them  <sub>[v2 c1 P45](../source/v02-c01.md#nw-v02-c01-p0045), [v2 c21 P36](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0036), [v2 c22 P9](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0009)</sub>
- withdrew to live in Echo Cottage after her mother died a decade ago  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076), [v2 c22 P7](../source/v02-c22.md#nw-v02-c22-p0007)</sub>
- hired a succession of young handmaidens whom she routinely calls Belinda regardless of their actual names  <sub>[v2 c21 P76](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0076)</sub>

## Quotes

> Each of you girls will get a cluster of lavender from me. Don’t you find it remarkably sweet? It was always a favorite of Mother’s.  <sub>[v2 c21 P86](../source/v02-c21.md#nw-v02-c21-p0086)</sub>

> Oh, at times, it seems to me that making friends serves no purpose. After a bit, they merely depart from your life, leaving behind an ache that exceeds the void existing before their arrival.  <sub>[v2 c27 P32](../source/v02-c27.md#nw-v02-c27-p0032)</sub>

> How silly and light-headed I have to be. It makes me thoroughly embarrassed that an untested gown . . . even one made of forget-me-not organdy . . . can thrill me in this way, whereas a clean conscience plus an increased donation to Foreign Missions failed to accomplish it.  <sub>[v2 c28 P19](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0019)</sub>

> Nell, do you and Hugh Carrow remain as close friends as you once were?  <sub>[v3 c23 P22](../source/v03-c23.md#nw-v03-c23-p0022)</sub>
